channel.description: An education daily: policy, vocational training, classroom technology and the business of learning.

item.title: Education Daily · November 13, 2026
item.description: Five stories today circle one question: what makes a credential count? China's human resources ministry has published a draft regulation on skills assessment - seven chapters, 63 articles, eight grade levels, with comment closing on December 12. In Wuhan a vice-minister sorted universities into research, applied and skills-oriented tracks while 16 school-enterprise deals were signed. Guangdong has 596 vocational schools and more than three million students, and is still working out whether they fit the factories. In Guizhou an eight-year-old was beaten with a ruler and the county conceded the punishment went too far. A Kuaishou charity, meanwhile, has packaged 30 AI classroom cases from rural schools. Certificates, categories and casebooks are all being rewritten at once. China consults on a skills-evaluation regulation: seven chapters, 63 articles and eight grade levels

item.title: Education Daily · November 12, 2026
item.description: Three stories today ask the same question from opposite ends: what makes a credential count? Seven ministries have moved engineers' continuing-education hours into a national registry and tied them to promotion. England's regulator says unsupervised assignments can no longer show what a student has learned, and wants more closed-book and oral assessment instead. Yunnan has rebuilt its vocational skills contest around 42 industry tracks, replacing the exam hall with a competition floor. Credits, hours and skill grades are being redefined at the same time. Seven ministries set continuing-education rules for engineers: six chapters, 29 articles, hours valid nationwide from January 1, 2027

item.title: Education Daily · November 11, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is that school places must follow the children. The NDRC is moving the basis for allocating places from household registration to the resident school-age population: kindergartens and compulsory schooling have peaked, vacated buildings are to be repurposed, and senior-high and higher education still need to expand. The skills side offers a different table: the national contest adds AI trainer and connected-vehicle trades, and a top-20 finish now buys a higher skill grade. Places are being reallocated while the skill standard is being redrawn. NDRC: school-age numbers have peaked for kindergartens and compulsory schooling, and senior-high places must follow the children

item.title: Education Daily · November 10, 2026
item.description: Today's thread: who gets the places, and who can prove it. Three ministries have turned the rural and poor-county admissions programme into a rural-revitalisation track covering 160 national and 390 provincial priority counties, and swapped a rural household registration for three years of actual study at a county high school. It starts with the 2030 intake. One year into the school science-education plan, the countable stock is 134 pilot districts, 1,246 pilot schools and more than 3,000 platform resources. Zhejiang's autumn job fair links 29,000 posts. Every policy ends up as a list someone has to verify. Rural-revitalisation admissions track confirmed: 160 national plus 390 provincial counties, applied from 2030

item.title: Education Daily · November 9, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is that places, jobs and courses all have to follow structural change. Yiwu is absorbing demographic waves with tidal schools: 7,650 places added and 14 more schools planned in five years. Hebei has put AI one-person companies into its graduate start-up support, while Hubei University of Automotive Technology has welded 58 undergraduate programmes to the car chain, with a 95% industry-match rate. The hard part for a school is not launching a new programme but letting old capacity, staffing and courses follow the students. Yiwu's tidal schools absorb enrolment waves: 7,650 places added, 14 more schools in five years

item.title: Education Daily · November 8, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is what time school starts, and who gets to teach. Cities are pushing arrival times back: Jiangyin primary schools at 8:00, middle schools at 7:40 and high schools at 7:20; a Chengdu primary moved to 8:40 from the start of winter; younger pupils at a Chongqing school arrive at 9:00, with first period at 9:45. On the same day, the NPC Standing Committee's vocational education law inspection team discussed its report, and the 2026 US-China Education Summit at Columbia put AI education and people-to-people exchange at the centre. A timetable is one notice; sleep, commuting and after-school care are what hold it up. Schools push back arrival and scrap morning reading: Jiangyin high schools at 7:20, a Chengdu primary at 8:40, Chongqing's youngest at 9:45 for first period

item.title: Education Daily · November 7, 2026
item.description: The thread today is who may teach and who gets a seat. The University of Chinese Academy of Social Sciences opened the country's first college for endangered disciplines — bachelor's to PhD, two supervisors — and gathered more than 80 institutions into an alliance. Shandong put forward six names for national school-aesthetics teacher studios, four of them from primary and secondary schools. The University of Science and Technology Beijing's Tianjin College signed up more than 20 companies for an AI industry-education alliance. Nameplates are cheap; posts, quotas and teaching hours are what someone pays for. UCASS opens the first college for endangered disciplines, with 80-plus institutions in its alliance

item.title: Education Daily · November 6, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is gatekeeping and who pays. Sichuan split supplementary materials into review, selection and purchase-on-behalf, effective December 5, with one set per subject and a six-month gate for out-of-catalogue items. Beijing set September 1, 2027 as the deadline to end delivered meals, convert all canteens to self-operation and build 1,000 smart canteens. The same week, Beijing released an AI-in-education package; its Zhi Xiaoyan platform is already in more than 100 schools with 30,000 users. Every gate ends with someone paying. Sichuan issues school-supplement rules: one set per subject, effective December 5

item.title: Education Daily · November 5, 2026
item.description: The word today is entry points. The education ministry took the four commonest gaokao registration scams apart one by one and repeated that registration, review, payment and eligibility run through a single provincial channel. In Hong Kong, 49 university presidents spent a day on what universities owe AI, society and civilisation, and 12 institutions signed agreements. Canada's teachers' federation drew four lines around AI in schools, and Guangxi used 33 skills events to photograph what employers now want. Fewer doors means fewer middlemen. Ministry warns 2027 gaokao applicants: four scam types, one official channel

item.title: Education Daily · November 4, 2026
item.description: The word of the day is eligibility. Jiangsu published the institutions and majors it proposes to authorise for bachelor's degrees — three institutions, 17 majors, 12 of them at two vocational universities. Yunnan proposed 20 pilot counties, 60 training bases and 600 priority schools for school football, basketball and volleyball, spread across 15 prefectures. On the employment side, the education ministry's regional tour closed in Changsha with 7,100 jobs and 1,623 first-round intentions from 5,000 graduates, while a Geely dual-study cohort in Ningbo has 97% of its first graduates already interning on the line. And in Haidian, a district-run agent platform now reaches more than 80 schools, 3,000 agents and 150,000 teachers and students. Eligibility decides who gets a seat; cost decides who keeps it. Jiangsu proposes three new degree-granting institutions and 17 majors, most of them vocational

item.title: Education Daily · November 3, 2026
item.description: Every education story today points the same way: how AI gets into the classroom. The Ministry of Education’s Fujiang programme opened in Guangxi — 14 cities, 20 counties, 60 schools — on the same day it ordered nationwide AI training for teachers; 81% say AI saves them preparation time, while the harder barrier turns out to be confidence, not skill. More than 700 companies brought "AI leads the way" as the theme to the national equipment fair. And 15 listed education companies reported 18.775 billion yuan of nine-month revenue — after two years of AI talk, delivery is starting to appear in the accounts. The threshold was never the hardware. Ministry of Education’s Fujiang programme launches in Guangxi: 14 cities, 20 counties, 60 schools
